newsitem.title: THAILAND: Gaddum says mark weakness a concern for Buba.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum says mark weakness a concern for Buba.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Thursday that the mark's weakness was a concern for the central bank.
"It is our concern at the moment ... that the markets are still in literal respect of the dollar ... is the development we have to mention," he told Reuters Financial Television.
"I once more underline, it is not in the interest of the Bundesbank that the strength of the dollar goes further and further," Gaddum said.
Gaddum is in Bangkok to attend a two-day Southeast Asian central bank governor's conference which opens today.

"I think the message from the Berlin (G7) meeting ... is no longer a situation of an overvalued mark," he said. "The government and the Bundesbank share the same concern on this point (mark weakness). There is no difference."
However, Gaddum said that the central bank was not looking for a specific level for the mark.
Traditionally Bundesbank policy was price-oriented and not exchange rate oriented, he told Reuters Financial Television. "I think therefore it is not accomodated to mention one figure."
Nevertheless, his comments saw the dollar slip against the yen and mark, with further long liquidation by traders and U.S. operators who had bought dollars earlier.
This pushed the dollar/mark lower and capped the dollar against the yen.
At 0344 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.6849/56 marks and 124.18/25 yen against the New York close of 1.6890/95 marks and 124.20/30 yen.
